newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela bolivar ends softer at 484/485/dlr.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela bolivar ends softer at 484/485/dlr.

text.p: A late spurt of corporate dollar demand weakened the Venezuelan bolivar to its 484.00/485.00 per dollar close in an otherwise quiet session that saw little Central Bank participation, traders said.
The unit closed last Friday at 483.50/484.50 per dollar.

"It was largely a quiet and slow day. It was only at the end of the day, when companies started wanting dollars and the Central Bank continued to stay away from the market, did the rate weaken," said one trader.

Venezuela's foreign exchange market is unusual in that the Central Bank is its largest single supplier of dollars, which blurs the difference between the Central Bank supplying liquidity and intervening.
However, some brokers saw the rate firming again Wednesday as foreign funds sell dollars to buy bolivars to participate in the Central Bank's 80 billion bolivar auction of TEM paper.
"Of course dollars are going to enter the market," said one.
